meta.title: Declining and then accepting: the latest answer wins in the vendor's event view
gaps: the decisive step tests something else than the case's point: The setup cannot create a live RFQ where the vendor has already declined at event level.
The required POST /user_intents decline and acceptance requests cannot be expressed because /user_intents is not an allowed request route; the acceptance is represented by library case EDGE-BID-009.
The event-view assertion can verify HTTP 200 but cannot verify an acceptance field because no event-view response field is provided.

words.preconditions: A fresh RFQ event, published, with one QA vendor invited; bidding open for about 20 minutes.
steps: The invited QA vendor sends the user intents request, exactly as the matching library case writes it.
As the invited QA vendor, read the request that reads the event and check that Status check: the reply's status code is 200 — OK — the request worked.
words.expected: The app accepts it. Read back afterwards: Status check: the reply's status code is 200 — OK — the request worked.
